body:
**P2: Optional v5 columns are now treated as mandatory**

The new schema check requires every column in `_V5_CORE_TABLE_COLUMNS` before calculating which `_V5_CORE_OPTIONAL_COLUMNS` are absent. This rejects supported pre-source-time schema-v5 stores as `schema_mismatch`, making the documented `source_time_unavailable` result unreachable for them. Retain the previous `required - optional <= columns` check while validating the newly covered tables, and add a regression with the optional source-time columns removed.

Category: Release regression

Why this matters: Operators lose all database findings for older but explicitly supported v5 copies instead of receiving findings with only view attribution marked unassessed.

**P2: Copy detection now discards meaningful source provenance**

Removing `source` from the duplicate-group key makes every source value equivalent, although the added test only establishes equivalence among legacy `NULL`/blank and `unknown` spellings. Two otherwise identical messages from distinct nonlegacy sources will now be grouped and may be reported as suspected or confirmed polluted copies. Normalize only the legacy spellings while retaining other source values, and test two distinct nonlegacy sources.

Category: Runtime correctness

Why this matters: The read-only inspector can falsely diagnose legitimate repeated messages as store pollution, undermining provenance-sensitive incident analysis.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Accept blank-owned rotation predecessors**

When a rotated legacy store has predecessor rows whose `conversation_id` is blank or NULL, every row passes the `owners` check but the additional `any(...)` still requires one row to contain the explicit selected conversation ID. Blank IDs are documented as belonging to the selected conversation, so an otherwise valid predecessor chain is rejected with `unverified_ancestry` and the inspector cannot report even its database findings. Treat the already-normalized blank ownership as sufficient for this predecessor validation.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the context-aware cap when checking leaf admission**

For a context of at least 50K tokens with `leaf_chunk_tokens` configured above 40% of that context, production clamps `_working_leaf_chunk_tokens()` to the context-aware cap. A raw backlog between that cap and the configured leaf size is therefore eligible for selection, but this check rejects it as `leaf_admission_unassessed` and suppresses all view-dependent findings. Derive the admission threshold from the captured `context_window` using the same cap as production rather than comparing only with `leaf_chunk_tokens`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Check mapping before rejecting composite candidates**

When a timestamped active user message exactly maps to a stored row whose content also happens to be a `"\n\n"` join of earlier stored texts, production maps that occurrence and `_identity_anchor_summary_input()` skips its composite-relation branch. This guard runs before mapping, detects the decomposition anyway, and returns `identity_anchor_unsupported`, suppressing all view findings for an ordinary stored replay. Build the mapping first and apply this composite guard only to unmapped messages with an eligible timestamp donor.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**P2: Optional v5 columns are now required**

The validator computes each table's optional columns but no longer subtracts them from the required set. Consequently, a supported pre-source-time v5 store missing fields such as `observed_at` or `observed_at_source` is rejected as `schema_mismatch`, making the documented `source_time_unavailable` path unreachable. Restore the optional-column subtraction when validating `_V5_CORE_TABLE_COLUMNS`.

Category: API compatibility

Why this matters: Operators cannot inspect valid older schema-v5 copies during wedge diagnosis.

**P2: Legacy predecessor rows fail ownership validation**

After accepting blank and NULL conversation IDs into `owners`, the rotation check additionally requires at least one predecessor row whose normalized conversation ID exactly equals the selected nonblank ID. A valid legacy predecessor containing only blank/NULL ownership values is therefore refused as `unverified_ancestry`, contradicting the documented rule that those values share the selected conversation's ownership. Accept an all-legacy predecessor when every row is otherwise owned, and add a rotation regression covering that shape.

Category: Runtime correctness

Why this matters: Valid rotated stores created from legacy rows cannot be inspected, precisely on the recovery path this tool is intended to support.

**P2: Optional v5 columns are now treated as mandatory**

The new full-schema check computes each table's permitted optional columns but then requires the entire `_V5_CORE_TABLE_COLUMNS` set. Consequently, a supported pre-source-time v5 store missing columns listed in `_V5_CORE_OPTIONAL_COLUMNS` is refused as `schema_mismatch` before `missing_optional` can drive the documented `source_time_unavailable` result. Require `required - optional <= columns` and add a regression using a v5 copy without the optional source-time columns.

Category: Migration

Why this matters: The operational inspector can no longer diagnose older supported v5 copies, precisely where migration and wedge investigation may be most important.

**Exclude unpersisted ignored messages from completeness.**

**`test_e1_prefix` "production" parity is tautological (confidence 85%).**

`_Probe` does not override `_store_complete_copy_twins`. It already inherits `StoreCompleteMixin._store_complete_copy_twins`. `_production_twins` puts back `_identity_anchor_owned` and `_host_uid_lineage_key` with the same behavior that `_Probe` already has (session-only ownership, `None` lineage). It then calls that same inherited method. The result is that `result == production` always holds, and the test does not check parity with the production engine. Only the `prefix_tokens == 14` and `prefix_rows == 2` assertions carry signal. Replace the monkeypatched comparison with a real `make_engine` run over the copied store, as `test_issue_1742_fix_r2.py` already does. One option is to assert `engine._store_complete_backlog` and the compress outcome against the inspector findings.

The key change is deliberate and matches production. The stored replay identity production uses to match view messages to store rows is (role, content, tool_call_id, tool_calls, tool_name), with no source. A generated store with identical rows tagged 'telegram' and 'discord' gives equal identities, and production maps a single view occurrence onto either row whatever its source. At 73300328 the inspector reports that pair as suspected, while the base key reported it as none even though production treats the rows as one identity. **P2: Optional v5 columns are now treated as mandatory**

This loop requires every column in `_V5_CORE_TABLE_COLUMNS`, even though `_V5_CORE_OPTIONAL_COLUMNS` explicitly permits pre-source-time v5 stores. Consequently, a supported store missing `observed_at` or another optional column is rejected as `schema_mismatch` before `missing_optional` can produce the documented `source_time_unavailable` result. Subtract `optional` from `required` as the previous implementation did, and add a regression using a v5 database without the optional source-time columns.

Category: API compatibility

Why this matters: The inspector loses all otherwise-available database findings for a documented, supported legacy schema shape.

**P2: Composite-donor lookup excludes legacy owned conversation spellings**

The inspector defines ownership elsewhere by normalizing `NULL`, blank, and padded conversation IDs, but this donor query only accepts the exact selected ID or `''`; the related `message_relations` queries are even narrower. A same-stamp user donor stored with `NULL`, whitespace, or a padded selected ID is therefore missed. An unmapped composite view message can then bypass `identity_anchor_unsupported` even though production may resolve it through the relation-writing identity-anchor path, allowing false view findings. Apply the same normalized ownership predicate used for `rows` to both direct and alternate-stamp donor queries, and cover NULL/blank/padded donors.

Category: Runtime correctness

Why this matters: The read-only inspector may report a complete or healthy view for an ownership spelling that production treats as eligible identity evidence.

False: the inspector's donor scope already matches production's. Production finds composite donors with MessageStore.find_rows_by_observed_at. Its direct query is `conversation_id IN (<stripped selected id>, '')` and its alternate-stamp query is `m.conversation_id = <stripped selected id>`. The stored column is not normalized, so a NULL, whitespace-only or padded row is never a donor in production. The inspector uses the same two predicates on the same stripped id and session, so it is not missing any donor that production uses. Current writers strip conversation ids and default them to '', so only legacy stores can hold these spellings.

Checked against generated stores at db9f0e06, with production compress run on a copy. In each store the view holds an unmapped user composite of two same-stamp rows:
- Donor rows NULL, whitespace or padded: production writes no composite relation and advances the frontier by rehydrating the hidden rows. The inspector reports healthy=false with view_state=unknown, so it never claims a healthy or complete view.
- One exact or '' donor plus one legacy-spelled constituent: production composes and writes the relation. The inspector refuses with identity_anchor_unsupported, because its candidate-text set already includes every normalized-owned row.
- Exact or '' donors: production writes the relation and the inspector refuses.
- Alternate-stamp aliases on non-exact rows: production writes no composite, the same as the inspector's exact-only alias query.
